tasks.short: Mark papers and assignments against the rubric, assess clinical and laboratory skills, record clinical results, score class quizzes, decide final grades, register them, and answer students' grade questions.

steps.what: Nursing instructor evaluates and grades assignments and papers against the rubric

loop.input: The student's paper, the rubric and the instructor's short notes per criterion.
loop.output: Draft feedback per rubric item for the instructor to edit.
loop.check: Code checks length, citation format and that every cited DOI resolves; each feedback item must quote a passage from the paper or it is dropped; the instructor checks that the quoted passage supports the item, sets every score and edits the text.
loop.stop: One draft per paper; items without a quoted passage are left for the instructor to write.
loop.why_not_simpler: Feedback must explain in prose what the paper does; fixed comment banks do not fit each paper.

steps.what: Nursing instructor assesses laboratory and clinic work with competency checklists
Nursing instructor records clinical assessment results: on paper forms today, on the tablet checklist after the change
Nursing instructor scores class work quizzes in a spreadsheet
Nursing instructor decides final grades as examiner
Nursing instructor checks the final grade list: each grade matches the decision and the component results
Nursing instructor types grades into the student administration system
Nursing instructor answers students' questions about grades

tasks.design: Papers come in through the learning environment ({LMS}); code checks length, citation format and DOIs, and a bounded step drafts rubric feedback from the instructor's notes, with each item quoting the paper. The instructor sets every score and edits the feedback. Clinical checklists are filled on a tablet during the assessment; this first record keeps its time. Closed quiz questions are marked by the learning environment. Once the instructor has decided and checked final grades as examiner, they pass to student administration ({OTHER}) without retyping. Grade questions are answered as today. No software sets a grade or judges clinical skill.
tasks.previous_blocker: Feedback was typed paper by paper, checklists were paper and grades typed into two systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Learning environments mark closed questions and draft rubric feedback; grade sync to student administration exists.
tasks.still_hard: Drafted feedback can sound right while missing the point of a paper.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a student's care at the bedside is safe.
tasks.altitude: The instructor edits feedback and decides grades instead of typing and tallying.

evidence.claim: FeedbackFruits gives formative feedback in the learning environment on criteria such as citation style; teachers edit the criteria.
At the University of Michigan, assistants edited FeedbackWriter's rubric suggestions in a randomised trial with 354 students and agreed with 88% of its judgments.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes is high-risk under Annex III point 3; here the instructor sets every score.
Examiners appointed by the examination board set results.

assumptions: Boundary: from student papers and placements to grade questions answered; fraud cases are outside.
Input contract: rubrics set by the instructor; papers in the learning environment; fallback is marking by hand.
Clinical assessment and grade decisions do not change.
A DPIA and works council consent come before use.
s5b and s6 are part of keeping grade records, which sibling task 25-1072.00:6133 covers; their saving is counted there, so they keep their full time here.
s1 keeps 70 because the instructor reads, scores and edits every paper; s3 is the first record of clinical results and keeps its full time; s4 keeps 30 for open quiz items; s7 keeps its full time.
research_questions: Do students act on drafted feedback as on hand-written feedback?

incremental.description: Nursing instructor writes notes per rubric item for the draft.

approvals.approved_version: The final grade per student exactly as decided by the examiner in s5 and checked in s5b, passed once to student administration; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: drafted feedback needs much editing, so s1 keeps 85 (11.2); high: drafts usable as assumed (16.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise students in the skills lab and on the ward, coordinate with ward nurses, record supervision notes and competency sign-offs, and schedule lab sessions.

steps.what: Nursing instructor supervises students' laboratory and clinical work
Nursing instructor coordinates with ward nurses about students
Nursing instructor records supervision notes and competency sign-offs: on paper today, in the e-portfolio on a phone after the change
Nursing instructor collects paper forms and types the notes and sign-offs into the student file; after the change only forms from wards without phone use are typed
Students book skills lab sessions in the shared calendar
Nursing instructor schedules laboratory sessions: in a spreadsheet today; after the change students book and the instructor sets capacity and handles clashes

tasks.design: Supervision notes and competency sign-offs go into the student's e-portfolio ({LMS}) on a phone, so paper forms are not collected and typed later. Students book skills lab sessions in a shared calendar ({CALENDAR}) with set capacity. Supervising at the bedside and in the lab, and agreeing with ward nurses, stay with the instructor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sign-offs were paper and lab sessions planned in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: E-portfolios work on phones; booking calendars handle capacity.
tasks.still_hard: Wards are busy and supervision time is short.
tasks.human_edge: Stepping in before a nervous student makes a medication error.
tasks.altitude: Less typing and scheduling; supervision stays.

reach.learn: Whether sign-offs are visible to the ward.

evidence.claim: E-portfolios on phones and booking calendars with capacity are common in nursing education.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student schedule to the sign-offs and lab schedule; placement allocation is outside.
Input contract: competency lists from the curriculum; fallback is paper forms and spreadsheets.
Supervising and agreeing with wards do not change.

Students book lab sessions in about the time it took to ask; their booking is shown in s3c. s3 is the first record and keeps its full time; s3b keeps 10 for paper forms from wards without phone use; s4 keeps 40 for capacity and clashes.
research_questions: Are sign-offs complete at the end of a placement more often?

incremental.description: Nursing instructor checks the lab booking calendar each week.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of the wards do not allow phones, so s3b keeps 50, and students still ask for sessions, so s4 keeps 70 (2.2); high: e-portfolio and booking as assumed (4.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare cases and questions for the discussion, moderate the classroom discussion, write a short summary, and post it in the learning environment.

steps.what: Nursing instructor prepares patient cases and questions to initiate discussions
Nursing instructor facilitates and moderates classroom discussions
Nursing instructor writes a short summary of the discussion in the summary template
Nursing instructor checks the final summary: it says what the class concluded and holds no patient details
Nursing instructor posts the checked summary on the course page

tasks.design: A shared case bank in the document space ({DOCS}) holds anonymised patient cases with questions per learning outcome, so instructors adapt cases instead of writing each one. The instructor writes the summary in a template after class, checks it and posts it once to the course page ({LMS}). Leading the discussion stays with the instructor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each instructor wrote their own cases.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared case banks are easy to keep in a document space.
tasks.still_hard: A good discussion depends on the group, not the case.
tasks.human_edge: Drawing out the quiet student who has seen this on placement.
tasks.altitude: Instructors adapt shared cases; leading the discussion stays.

evidence.claim: Shared case banks in document spaces let teachers reuse and adapt cases.

assumptions: Boundary: from the lesson plan to the summary posted; exams are outside.
Input contract: cases anonymised and added by the teaching team; fallback is writing own cases.
Students read the summary as they would class notes; no added student time.
s1 keeps 70 for adapting cases; s3 keeps 85 because the template gives only the layout; s4 keeps 20 for posting.

incremental.description: Nursing instructor adds new cases to the shared bank.

approvals.approved_version: The discussion summary exactly as checked by the instructor in s3b, posted once on the course page for this class; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the shared bank holds few cases for this course, so s1 keeps 90 (5.4); high: the bank covers most topics as assumed (9.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review students' portfolios and results, talk with ward staff and students, survey students and preceptors, decide education needs and priorities, write the needs report, and send it to the curriculum committee.

steps.what: Nursing instructor reviews competence portfolios and results to assess clinical education needs
Nursing instructor talks with ward staff and students about patient teaching needs
Students fill in the online needs survey
Preceptors fill in the online needs survey
Nursing instructor surveys students and preceptors and tallies answers: on paper today, online with automatic tallies after the change
Nursing instructor decides education needs and priorities
Nursing instructor writes the education needs report
Nursing instructor checks the final needs report: figures match the dashboard and the priorities say what was decided
Nursing instructor sends the checked needs report to the curriculum committee

tasks.design: A dashboard ({BI}) from the e-portfolios shows which competences students sign off late or rarely, so the instructor sees gaps without reading every portfolio. The survey moves online with automatic tallies. The needs report uses a template with the dashboard figures filled in, and the instructor checks it and sends it once to the curriculum committee. Talking with wards and students and deciding priorities stay with the instructor; the dashboard shows groups, not single students.
tasks.previous_blocker: Portfolios were read one by one and survey forms tallied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: E-portfolios feed dashboards; online surveys tally answers.
tasks.still_hard: What wards need changes faster than the curriculum.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing from a ward sister what new graduates cannot yet do.
tasks.altitude: The instructor reads gaps and decides instead of counting.

evidence.claim: E-portfolio data can feed dashboards; online surveys tally answers.

assumptions: Boundary: from student portfolios to the report sent; curriculum decisions are outside.
Input contract: sign-offs in e-portfolios; fallback is reading portfolios and paper surveys.

Students and preceptors fill the online survey in about the time the paper one took; their answers are shown in s2b and s2c. s1 keeps 50 for reading the gaps; s3 keeps 40 for writing questions and reading tallies; s5 keeps 70 because the template gives figures and layout; checking and sending the report keep their full time.
Talks and priority decisions do not change.
research_questions: Do gaps found by the dashboard match what wards report?

incremental.description: Nursing instructor checks dashboard figures against portfolios.

approvals.approved_version: The needs report with figures and priorities exactly as checked by the instructor in s5b, sent once to the curriculum committee; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few sign-offs are in e-portfolios yet, so portfolios are still read and s1 keeps 80 (15.6); high: dashboard as assumed (23.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The nursing instructor keeps supervising at the bedside, leading discussions, judging skills and deciding grades; typed feedback, paper sign-offs and tallies shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An instructor with more time on the ward with students.
